summary: Horizontal 2x interpolating pixel filter. For each of the row-count rows (field +0x110 on a1), reads an input row pointer from array a3[i] and an output row pointer from (*a4)[i], then writes 2*count output bytes per row from count input bytes using weighted kernel arithmetic ((3a+b+2)>>2, (a+3b+1)>>2 etc.): first output byte copied through, interior runs as a (count-2)-iteration loop when the channel count at a2+40 differs from 2, and the trailing boundary always emitted. Returns a1. The a2+40 != 2 guard skips the interior loop for the 2-channel case, leaving only boundary pixels processed.

local_names.a1: filter object holding the row count at +0x110
local_names.a2: object whose channel count is read at +0x28 (a2+40)
local_names.a3: array of input pixel row pointers, one per row
local_names.a4: pointer to the array of output pixel row pointers
local_names.v5: current output row pointer entry of (*a4)
local_names.v7: byte distance from v5 to a3, kept constant so v8 = a3[i] as the row counter advances

operations.description: initialize row counter v18 = 0 and load the output row-pointer array v5 = *a4
enter the per-row loop only when the row count at a1 + 272 (> 0x110) is greater than 0; otherwise return a1 unchanged
precompute v7 = a3 - v5 once; per row, v8 = *(BYTE**)(v5 + v7) resolves to the input row pointer a3[rowIndex] as v5 advances
iterate rows while v18 < row count at a1+272; per row write the leading boundary pixels out[0] = in[0] and out[1] = (3*in[0] + in[1] + 2) >> 2
when the channel count at a2 + 40 is not 2, process the interior pixels with the weighted blend loop
interior loop of (channel count - 2) iterations; each iteration emits two outputs from three adjacent inputs: out[2k] = (in[k-1] + 3*in[k] + 1) >> 2 and out[2k+1] = (in[k+1] + 3*in[k] + 2) >> 2
emit the trailing boundary pixels out[2*count-2] = (in[count-2] + 3*in[count-1] + 1) >> 2 and out[2*count-1] = in[count-1]
